```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"The current federal budget deficit is nearly $1.4 trillion, which is 10 percent of GDP.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Most economists, both conservative and liberal, believe that half of the current federal budget deficit was caused by counter-cyclical spending to combat the financial crisis of 2008 and the ensuing Great Recession.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The federal budget deficit will shrink as the economy recovers, job growth resumes, and personal incomes rise.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Approximately $700 billion of the current federal budget deficit resulted from the Reagan and Bush tax cuts, the failure to raise taxes to finance two wars, and a profit-driven health system that drives up costs for Medicare and Medicaid.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Reversing the Bush tax cuts would yield $125 billion in additional federal revenue per year.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Restoring corporate and income tax rates to those of the Eisenhower era would yield another $300 billion in revenue per year.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Eliminating weapons programs and reducing the number of foreign military bases (more than 200) would yield another $200-300 billion in yearly revenues.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"A modest transaction tax of 0.25 percent on all financial trading could raise over $600 billion in annual revenue and tamp down destabilizing financial speculation.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```

```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"The current federal budget deficit is nearly $1.4 trillion, which is 10 percent of GDP.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Most economists, both conservative and liberal, believe that half of the current federal budget deficit was caused by the counter-cyclical spending required to combat the financial crisis of 2008 and the ensuing Great Recession.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The deficit will shrink as the economy recovers, job growth resumes, and personal incomes rise.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The remainder of the current deficit, some $700 billion, was largely the result of the Reagan and Bush tax cuts, the failure to raise taxes to finance two wars, and a profit-driven health system that drives up costs for Medicare and Medicaid.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Reversing the Bush tax cuts would yield $125 billion in additional federal revenue per year.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Restoring corporate and income tax rates to those of the Eisenhower era would yield another $300 billion in revenue per year.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Eliminating weapons programs we no longer need and reducing our more than 200 foreign military bases would yield another $200-300 billion in yearly revenues.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"A modest transaction tax of 0.25 percent on all financial trading could raise over $600 billion in annual revenue and tamp down destabilizing financial speculation.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
